pages.title: How to talk about taboo topics and how to separate from your identity.
pages.full_content:
Procedure:

Why would you want to separate from your identity? Perhaps in order to create a new identity. Ultimately, the best spies can hide themselves as insiders which allow them to "freeride" to get information. One of the best ways to understand and communicate the identity of someone in another culture is to practice the old school debate team exercise of arguing both sides of an argument.

Wednesday assignment- long reading, also presented as a google form right in this page. This will require you to read the textbook. That assignment is due Friday 10 PM. It is going to be about Chapter 7. Look at your identities. How are these identites being shaped (gender, race, ethnic, organizational) by what is happening? Someone noted that their sports team connections were starting to drift apart. This is a way that you might be experiencing a shift in your organizational identity. I asked you to create an alias and a name for your cohort. In this way, I wanted you to play with different types of personal identities. How is your identity helping you or hindering you in coping with what is going on? I am noticing, for instance, that some people are shining online in their work in a way that they may not have in the classroom where others. Anyway, that's work for Friday.

Saturday assignment- your day-by-day log on what you've observed about the week. This week, I want you to notice play. Notice changes in the way you play, what you observe on the street, and challenge yourself to see if you can incorporate play into the life of your Core 5. Here's a bonus. Learn to play poker and play it with people (if you can).

One of the keys in communicating with other cultures comes in discovering how, even when your venn diagram doesn't intersect the venn diagram of someone else's culture you're still able to communicate that you understand what the other person is saying. One way to do this is to do something called reflective listening this is how it works:

"I'm so proud of myself. I have not watched a second of the hearings nor have I watched the fake news in weeks. Those of you who know me well are aware that this feat is a miracle. I'll be sure to get out to vote TRUMP 2020! Life is great!"

To listen reflectively, you can say, "So what you're saying is that you are not watching the news which is a great accomplishment of self-control for you. You definitely support Trump, and you're feeling that life is great. Am I hearing you right?"

The person confirms. You ask if they have more to explain or if you got it.

The next step is to move to the affect reflection. "That must make you feel so free and confident about your decisions."

Wait for a response. Finally, you can say, "I can understand that if you support Trump all this news could just bring you down and not watching the news would make you feel good. That makes lots of sense."

You have validated the person without necessarily agree with the person to validate their opinion.

Your cohort's task today is to practice validation. One of you will play the role of choosing a controversial opinion. It doesn't matter if you believe the opinion or not. Take some time to think about a reasonable argument to make for the position you choose (going to offer some doozies). The job of the other person is just to reflect and validate the opinion of the other person without necessarily agreeing.

Station #1:

Take a minute or two to think of a one to two minute argument supporting one of these ideas:

  1. The coronavirus is invented by aliens who want to delay us from getting to Mars.
  2. The world is actually flat.
  3. College tuition is too low and should be raised.
  4. People can actually live underwater for an hour if they believe they can.

The job of the talker is to express the idea to the cohort. The job of the listener is to listen actively and reflect what the person is saying back to them, and to validate what they're saying without agreeing or disagreeing or judging.

The rest of the cohort will act as judges to determine if the listener was objective without ceeding agreement. You have a minute, and then you'll switch until everyone has a chance to be the talker and the listener.

Station #2:

Reading.. So, what does this have to do with identity? You need to be strong in your own identity to be able to validate others.

Before class: If you arrive early, you can read the (translated from Hungarian) lyrics before listening to the song and discuss with other students (or just socialize!). Based on the lyrics, how do you imagine the song will sound?

Do you still think about our little village
About the boy next door, who is still waiting?
A kiss at the end of the garden if you sneak
Under our willow trees, where no one sees
As the suns turned
The fire of our kiss would ignite.
This is how winter hides in the fall
Our love reaches the sky
Blood red at dusk
It trickles under the trees
I search, but you're not here
Conflict arises, tears us apart
Hey ná ná hé ná ná
It was a long time ago, yet it transfixes me
Hey ná ná hé ná ná
Wherever you go, you live in me
A thousand years is only one day and
One hundred borders are just a step
Hey ná ná hé ná ná
Wherever you go, you live in me
Years go by and I don't see you
There is no laughter from the house next door
At the end of the garden, lights are on
Iron gate and willow fence
Wherever you go, you live in me.
